html:
A novel in Arabic by the Sudanese writer Tayeb Salih, published in 1966. It is often named the most important Arabic novel of the 20th century.

The narrator comes home to his village on the Nile in Sudan after years of study in England. There he meets a stranger, Mustafa Sa'eed, who turns out to have lived a dark life in London: a brilliant student who seduced English women, several of whom killed themselves, and who was jailed for murdering his wife. Mustafa's story, and his disappearance, pull the narrator into a crisis of his own.

The book turns the journey of Joseph Conrad's Heart of Darkness around: here an African goes into the heart of Europe. It deals with colonialism, desire and violence, and with the gap between the West and the village. The translation by Denys Johnson-Davies in 1969 brought it to English readers. It was banned in Sudan for a time for its sexual scenes. It is read alongside the novels of Chinua Achebe as a classic of writing after empire.
sum: A novel in Arabic by the Sudanese writer Tayeb Salih, published in 1966. It is often named the most important Arabic novel of the 20th century.
